threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, governance and initial priorities for the initiative.

messages.text: Welcome all to this channel for our Sustainable Housing Portfolio Optimisation Initiative. Over the next 30 days we need a clear scope, success metrics, and a simple way to steer decisions. I have drafted a first outline of the operating model and case in the doc linked as Sustainable Housing Operating Model and Business Case, which will become artifact A2 and is tied to task T2. In parallel, I would like us to use the governance charter draft, artifact A8, as the basis for task T9 on governance and decision rights. Proposal: this thread focuses on confirming scope and success metrics for the first 30 days and agreeing how we make decisions and report progress. I will summarise decisions under D1 and D2 once we converge.

Thanks for kicking this off. For scope, I suggest we keep the first 30 days focused on three things: 1) baseline and quick diagnostic, 2) target operating model and business case in A2 under T2, and 3) governance and reporting structure in A8 under T9. For success metrics in this first window, I would propose: a) sign-off on the business case assumptions, b) agreement on a shortlist of phase 1 properties, and c) a simple KPI set and dashboard mock-up outline, which will later be formalised under T5. Does that feel realistic given the constraints and the board expectation of early results?

From the housing side, I can commit in the first 30 days to mapping the current portfolio performance for T1 and starting T6 on prioritising buildings. I will need clarity on which metrics matter most for the scope. Right now we track occupancy and rent, but service issues are logged differently by each site. For success metrics, would it be enough if we have a complete list of properties with occupancy and rent, plus at least a first pass on the top recurring tenant issues, so that can feed into A2 and the later dashboard?

On governance and scope, from a quality and audit angle I suggest we include in the first 30 days at least a draft of the quality and compliance checklist for T4 and a simple pre-audit plan for pilots under T8. That way A4 and A7 can start to take shape early, even if we only execute the full audits slightly later. For success metrics, maybe we can say that by day 30 we have: a) a draft checklist, b) agreement on which properties will be used as pilots, and c) a basic remediation workflow defined with the housing team.

From the green ICT side, I would like the first 30 days scope to explicitly include: 1) a prioritised list of green ICT initiatives for T3, and 2) a draft communication plan for tenants and staff under T7. That means at least a first version of A3 and A6. For success metrics, I would track: a) agreement on which ICT initiatives are in phase 1, b) confirmation that the roadmap integrates with existing systems at a high level, and c) sign-off on the initial communication approach so we can manage tenant expectations early.

Let me try to synthesise what we have so far into a proposed 30 day scope. Scope items: 1) Baseline and diagnostic: T1, early view for T6, and initial quality lens from T4 and T8. 2) Target model and business case: T2, with inputs from housing, quality, and ICT. 3) Governance and reporting: T9, plus a first outline of the KPI dashboard structure under T5 so we can show the board how we will track progress. Success metrics for this period: a) A2 drafted and agreed at working group level, b) A8 finalised and acknowledged, c) shortlist of phase 1 properties and services agreed in principle, and d) initial KPI list and dashboard mock-up structure defined. If we align on this, I will record it under D1 as our scope and success metrics for the first 30 days.

The synthesis looks good to me. One nuance: for the KPI dashboard under T5 and artifact A5, I would keep the first 30 days to defining the KPI list, formulas, and data sources, plus a rough mock-up. The actual build can follow once we have more stable data from T1 and T3. For D1, I would phrase the success metric as: by day 30 we have a working group approved draft of A2 and A8, a documented shortlist of phase 1 properties, and a KPI list with owners and data sources.

I am aligned with that scope. For the shortlist of phase 1 properties, I will start from the occupancy and rent data for T1 and then add a simple view of service issues, even if the logging is not perfect yet. That should be enough for us to have a first pass list for T6 within the 30 days. For D1, I just want to confirm that we are not expected to have tenant facing changes live in this period, only the plan and priorities.

I am comfortable with this framing. For the ICT part, I will keep the first 30 days focused on defining and sequencing initiatives in A3 and aligning dependencies with existing systems, not on implementation. That will give us enough clarity for the business case in A2 without creating integration risk too early. For D1, I would add that we should have at least a draft of the communication plan A6, even if we only finalise it once the pilot properties are locked.

From my side, I confirm that within 30 days I can deliver a draft of the checklist for A4 under T4 and a simple audit plan for T8, even if the full audits happen slightly later. That will support both A2 and A8. I agree that tenant facing changes should not be in scope yet; we should first make sure our internal processes and governance are clear.

On governance and decision rights, the draft A8 for T9 proposes a steering group with myself and one representative from each area, plus a working group that meets more frequently. Decision rights: 1) strategic scope, budget envelope, and major trade-offs sit with the steering group, 2) operational decisions on pilots, process changes, and ICT phasing sit with the working group, within the agreed constraints, and 3) any regulatory or tenant impact risk is escalated to the steering group. Reporting: weekly written update in this channel and a short steering note every two weeks. If there are no objections, I will record this under D2 as our governance structure and decision rights.

The governance proposal works for me. One practical suggestion: for the weekly written update, I can take the lead on a short summary post that captures progress on T1 to T4, T6, T7, and any key risks or decisions, and then you can forward highlights to the board as needed. That will also help keep A2 and A8 aligned with reality as we learn from the pilots.

I am ok with that structure. For escalations on tenant impact, I will make sure any major change in service levels or communication is flagged early so it can go to the steering group. For the working group, I suggest we include at least one site supervisor so that the decisions on T1, T6, and T12 are grounded in day to day operations.

No objections from me. The split between steering and working group is clear. For ICT topics under T3 and T7, I will treat the working group as the main decision forum, and only bring items to the steering group when they affect budget envelope, regulatory exposure, or tenant experience at scale.

I support the governance proposal. For quality and audits, I will use the working group to validate the checklist A4 and the audit approach for T8 and T12, and escalate only if we see systemic issues that could affect compliance or reputation.

Given the alignment in this thread, I will formalise two decisions. First, under D1, we confirm that the scope for the first 30 days covers: baseline and diagnostic (T1, early T6, T4, T8), target operating model and business case (T2), and governance and reporting (T9, early T5). Success metrics: draft A2 and A8 agreed at working group level, shortlist of phase 1 properties and services documented, and initial KPI list and dashboard structure outlined in A5. Second, under D2, we confirm the governance structure described in A8 for T9: steering group for strategic and high impact decisions, working group for operational decisions within constraints, with weekly written updates and bi-weekly steering notes. I will update A2 and A8 accordingly and share the links.
Thanks for capturing D1 and D2. I will start updating A2 with the agreed scope and success metrics and sketch the KPI list for A5 so that we can review it in the next standup.
I will move ahead on T1 and T6 with this scope in mind and share a first cut of the baseline so it can feed into A2 and the governance discussions.

threads.thread_goal: Review housing portfolio baseline and select phase 1 pilot properties.

messages.text: I have uploaded the first version of the Housing Portfolio Performance Baseline as artifact A1, linked to T1. It lists all properties with occupancy, rent levels, and the service issues I could consolidate from different logs. I have also drafted an initial shortlist for T6, focusing on buildings with lower occupancy and more frequent service complaints. Before we lock the phase 1 pilots, I would like your feedback on the selection and on the criteria we should use for later phases.

Thanks for pulling A1 together. Looking at the data, I see three clusters: 1) high occupancy, stable rent, low issues; 2) mid occupancy with some service noise; 3) low occupancy and high issue rates. For T6, I would propose that phase 1 pilots come mainly from cluster 3, with maybe one or two from cluster 2 where we see clear sustainability upside. For later phases, criteria could include impact on revenue, cost to improve, and readiness of local teams. We should also consider how representative the pilots are for the wider portfolio so that A2 and A5 are based on realistic assumptions.

From a quality and audit perspective, I would like at least two of the phase 1 pilots to be properties where we already have some incident history, so that T8 and A7 can capture before and after effects. Also, for T12, it would help if we include one site with more complex incident patterns so we can stress test the standardised process. For criteria, I suggest we add compliance risk and safety criticality alongside occupancy and service issues.

Looking at A1 with an ICT and sustainability lens, I would prioritise buildings where we can deploy energy monitoring and digital communication with relatively low integration effort. For T3 and T7, that means sites where connectivity is stable and where tenants already use some digital channels. Maybe we can tag each property in A1 with a simple readiness score for ICT so that T6 can balance impact and feasibility.

That makes sense. In my initial shortlist for T6 I focused mostly on low occupancy and high complaints, but I did not factor in ICT readiness or compliance risk explicitly. I can go back to A1 and add two extra columns: one for a simple ICT readiness score, based on input from ICT, and one for a rough compliance or safety concern flag based on past incidents. Then we can re-rank the shortlist before we decide on D3 and D4.

Good plan. For the criteria that will later support D4, I suggest we formalise them as: 1) occupancy and revenue impact, 2) service quality and tenant experience, 3) sustainability and ICT potential, 4) compliance and safety risk, and 5) operational readiness of local teams. We can then assign simple scores in A1 and use that to justify the phase 1 list for D3 and the approach for later phases in A2.

I like the structured criteria. For the compliance and safety risk dimension, I can review A1 and cross check with our incident records to flag properties where T8 and T12 should focus first. That will also help us plan the use of A4 and A7 in the pilots.

For the sustainability and ICT potential dimension, I can propose a simple scoring model for T3: for each property in A1 we rate connectivity, existing digital usage, and potential energy savings. That will feed into A3 and help us pick pilots where we can show early wins without heavy integration work.

This is heading in the right direction. Before we lock D3 and D4, I want to be sure we are not overloading any single site and that we respect the constraint of minimal disruption to tenants. For phase 1 pilots under T6, I would prefer a small but diverse set of properties where we can manage change carefully. For later phases, the criteria you are defining should help us scale in a controlled way. Once you have updated A1 with the extra scores, please propose a concrete phase 1 list and a short note on the criteria so I can review and confirm.

Understood. I will update A1 with the ICT readiness and compliance flags and then refine the T6 shortlist to a small, diverse set of properties. I will also draft a short note summarising the criteria we used, aligned with what was proposed for D4. I will share both here for review before we confirm D3 and D4.

Once you share the refined shortlist, I can run a quick financial view on each candidate using the data in A1 and our assumptions in A2. That will help us see which combination of pilots gives us the best balance of impact and feasibility for D3.

I have now updated A1 with the ICT readiness and compliance flags and refined the T6 shortlist to five candidate properties: two with low occupancy and high issues, two with mid occupancy and strong sustainability potential, and one with complex incident patterns. Based on the criteria we discussed, my proposal for phase 1 pilots is to select three of these: one from each type, so we cover different situations without overloading operations.

From the quality side, I support that mix. It gives us one property where we can test improvements on frequent issues, one where we can focus on sustainability and ICT, and one where we can refine the incident and damage assessment process under T12. I do not see any compliance blockers for these three based on our current records.

I checked the three proposed pilots against our ICT constraints. All of them have acceptable connectivity and some level of digital usage, so they are suitable for the first wave of T3 and T7. This will allow us to test the green ICT roadmap in A3 and the communication plan in A6 without heavy custom work.

I ran a quick financial comparison using A1 and the assumptions in A2. The three proposed pilots give us a good spread of potential revenue uplift and cost savings, while keeping the initial investment manageable. They also provide useful data points for T11 later on. I recommend we go ahead with this set for D3.

Based on your inputs, I am comfortable confirming the three proposed properties as our phase 1 pilots under T6. I will record this under D3 as the approved list of phase 1 pilot properties and services. For D4, we also confirm the prioritisation criteria as: occupancy and revenue impact, service quality and tenant experience, sustainability and ICT potential, compliance and safety risk, and operational readiness. These criteria will guide later phases and will be documented in A2 and reflected in A1.
I will update T6 and A1 to mark the three selected properties as phase 1 pilots and inform the local teams so they can prepare for the upcoming audits and ICT changes.
I will reflect D3 and D4 in A2 and use the agreed criteria to shape the phasing assumptions for later waves in the business case.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the green ICT roadmap and communication plan.

messages.text: I have posted a draft of the Green ICT Roadmap and Integration Overview as artifact A3, linked to T3. It outlines three waves of initiatives: 1) energy monitoring and basic tenant portal enhancements in the phase 1 pilot properties, 2) broader rollout of digital communication tools, and 3) optimisation and analytics. In parallel, I have started a draft Tenant and Staff Communication Plan as artifact A6 under T7, focusing first on the three pilot properties we agreed in D3. I would like to use this thread to align on which initiatives go into phase 1 for D5 and to finalise the communication plan for D6.

Looking at A3, the first wave seems manageable from an operations point of view, but I want to be careful about how many changes hit the sites at once. For phase 1 under D5, I would prefer we focus on energy monitoring and a small set of tenant portal improvements that directly address the main service issues we saw in A1, rather than a full set of new features. For A6, we need clear messages for staff on what is changing in their daily routines.

From a business case angle, the initiatives in wave 1 of A3 that have the clearest short term impact are: basic energy monitoring, digital notices instead of paper, and simple self service options for common requests. For D5, I would suggest we include only those in phase 1, and leave more advanced analytics and automation for later waves. That will also keep the integration work lighter and align with the budget constraints we are discussing under T10.

For quality and audits, I want to make sure that any new digital tools in phase 1 can support consistent incident reporting and follow up. If we include a basic incident reporting feature in the tenant portal as part of T3, we should align it with the standard process we are defining under T12 and the checklist in A4. That way A7 will capture comparable data across the pilot properties.

That is a good point. For phase 1 under D5, I can narrow the scope in A3 to: 1) install or activate energy monitoring for the three pilot properties, 2) enable digital notices and basic messaging to tenants, and 3) add a simple incident reporting form aligned with T12. We would postpone more complex portal features and analytics to later waves. For A6, I will make sure we have a clear section for staff explaining what changes in their daily work and what stays the same.

If we keep phase 1 to those three items, I am comfortable from an operations side. For A6, I would like to see concrete examples of tenant messages, especially around energy monitoring, so we do not create confusion or unrealistic expectations. Also, we should clarify in the plan who answers tenant questions about the new tools.

With that narrower phase 1 scope, I can update A2 to reflect the cost and benefit profile more accurately. It will also make it easier to align with the budget envelope in T10. For D5, I support the proposal to include only energy monitoring, digital notices, and basic incident reporting in phase 1.

I agree with that phase 1 set. For the incident reporting form, I will share the draft process from T12 so we can align the fields. That will help ensure that A7 captures the right information for audits and follow up.

On A6, I have drafted example messages for tenants explaining: 1) why we are introducing energy monitoring, 2) what data is collected and how it is protected, and 3) how they can use the portal for notices and incident reporting. For staff, there is a section on how to respond to common questions and where to escalate issues. Please review and let me know if the tone and level of detail work for your teams.

I have reviewed A6. The messages are clear, but I suggest we add a short note for tenants about who to contact if they prefer not to use digital channels, so we do not alienate those who are less comfortable online. For staff, it would help to include a simple checklist they can use when explaining the changes during on site conversations.

From a risk and stakeholder angle, I would also add in A6 a brief reference to how this supports our sustainability targets and what benefits tenants can expect, such as more responsive service and potentially lower energy costs over time. That will help with adoption and will be useful when we report progress in A5.

Good suggestions. I will update A6 to: 1) include an alternative contact path for tenants who do not want to use digital tools, and 2) add a short checklist for staff to guide their conversations. I will also incorporate the sustainability and benefit framing suggested, so that the messages are consistent with the business case in A2.

To close this out, let me restate what I hear for D5 and D6. For D5, phase 1 of the green ICT roadmap in A3 under T3 will include: energy monitoring for the three pilot properties, digital notices and basic messaging, and a simple incident reporting form aligned with T12. More advanced features and analytics will be deferred to later waves. For D6, we will approve A6 as the tenant and staff communication plan for the first rollout, once the updates you just discussed are in place. This plan will cover the three pilot properties, with clear messages, alternative contact options, and staff guidance.
That summary matches my understanding. With that phase 1 scope, I can plan staff briefings at the pilot sites and coordinate with local teams so they are ready when the tools go live.

I will now update A3 and A6 to reflect the agreed phase 1 scope and communication details and then mark T3 and T7 phase 1 design as ready for implementation planning. Once that is done, we can treat D5 and D6 as confirmed.
Confirmed. With the updates to A3 and A6, we formally approve D5 and D6 as described. This gives us a clear, focused ICT and communication package for the pilots that fits within our constraints.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on quality, compliance and audit approach for pilot properties.

messages.text: I have shared a draft of the Housing Quality and Compliance Checklist as artifact A4, linked to T4. It covers safety, service quality, and basic sustainability criteria. I also uploaded initial findings from baseline checks on the three pilot properties into A7, which will evolve into the Pilot Property Audit and Incident Log under T8. In this thread, I would like us to agree on the standard checklist for pilots for D7 and decide on remediation priorities for the issues already identified for D8.

Thanks for pulling A4 and A7 together. The checklist looks comprehensive, but I am concerned it might be heavy for site teams to use in one go. For the pilots under T8, could we split A4 into a core section that must be done every time and an extended section that we use less frequently? That might help with adoption while we standardise T12.

From a governance and cost perspective, I would like A4 to clearly distinguish between mandatory compliance items and improvement opportunities. That will help us prioritise remediation under D8 and link the actions to the business case in A2. In A7, it would be useful to tag each finding with severity and estimated cost to fix, even if the numbers are rough at this stage.

Looking at A4, I suggest we add a few simple checks related to ICT and digital tools, such as availability of connectivity in common areas and basic device security practices. That will support T3 and ensure that when we roll out the green ICT initiatives, we are not creating new risks.

Good feedback. I can restructure A4 into three parts: 1) mandatory compliance and safety checks, 2) core service quality checks, and 3) optional sustainability and ICT checks. For the pilots under T8, we can require parts 1 and 2 every time and use part 3 where relevant. I will also incorporate the ICT items suggested so that T3 is covered.

On A7, I will add severity levels and a rough cost estimate for each finding, using input from housing and finance where needed. That will help us prioritise remediation for D8 and feed into A2. I will also flag which findings are directly linked to the standard incident and damage assessment process we are defining in T12.

Splitting A4 that way will help a lot. For the pilots, I can make sure site teams focus on the mandatory and core sections first. For the optional sustainability and ICT checks, we can schedule them when we have support from your team and ICT, so they do not get skipped.

Once you have updated A7 with severity and cost, I can help group the remediation actions into quick wins, medium, and larger investments. That will support D8 and also inform the phasing in A2 and the budget work under T10.

For the optional sustainability and ICT checks in A4, I can provide a short guide so that site teams know what to look for, especially around connectivity and device usage. That will make the data more consistent and useful for T3.

I have now updated A4 with the three part structure and added the ICT related checks. For A7, I have tagged the main findings in the three pilot properties with severity and rough cost estimates. The most critical issues are: 1) safety related items in two properties, 2) recurring service delays in one property, and 3) a few sustainability opportunities with moderate cost. We should now agree on remediation priorities for D8.

From an operations and tenant perspective, I would prioritise remediation as follows: first, all safety related issues, even if they require some disruption; second, the recurring service delays, which are driving complaints; and third, the sustainability opportunities where we can bundle work with other planned maintenance. This order should be reflected in D8.

I agree with that order. It also aligns with cost effectiveness: safety issues are non negotiable, service delays often have a clear impact on satisfaction and occupancy, and sustainability upgrades can be phased. For D8, we can define three remediation waves: immediate safety fixes, short term service improvements, and planned sustainability upgrades, all documented in A7 and reflected in A2.

For the sustainability related findings, I suggest we align them with the green ICT roadmap in A3 so that we do not create overlapping work. Some of the upgrades might be better handled as part of the ICT and energy monitoring rollout under T3 rather than as standalone remediation.

On D7, I propose that we approve the updated A4 as the standard quality and compliance checklist for the pilot properties under T4 and T8, with the three part structure you described. On D8, we will set remediation priorities as: 1) immediate action on all safety related findings, 2) targeted fixes for recurring service delays, and 3) phased sustainability upgrades aligned with the ICT roadmap. These priorities should be clearly recorded in A7 and reflected in the implementation plan.

I will mark A4 as the approved checklist for pilots and update A7 to clearly label the remediation actions according to the three priority waves we agreed for D8. I will also coordinate with housing to schedule the immediate safety fixes.

I will work with site teams to implement the safety and service related remediation actions in the pilots and make sure they use A4 consistently. For T12, I will also adjust the incident and damage assessment process so that it lines up with the new checklist and A7.

threads.thread_goal: Lock budget envelope, KPI dashboard and reporting cadence.

messages.text: I have shared the Executive KPI and Sustainability Dashboard Mock up as artifact A5, linked to T5. It includes proposed KPIs for occupancy, tenant satisfaction, service quality, sustainability, and financial performance. I also prepared initial budget scenarios for the first year, aligned with T10 and the efficiency gains we expect from T11. In this thread, we need to confirm the KPI set and dashboard structure for D9 and agree on the budget allocation and phasing for D10.

Looking at A5, the occupancy and service quality KPIs are straightforward for us to track from A1 and our logs. For tenant satisfaction, we will need to standardise how we collect feedback across properties. For D9, I would like to keep the number of KPIs that site teams have to report on manageable, otherwise we risk inconsistent data.

For sustainability and ICT, I propose we include in A5 a small set of KPIs: energy consumption per occupied unit in the pilots, share of tenant interactions handled digitally, and basic system uptime for the new tools. These can be sourced from A3, A6, and the systems we deploy under T3 and T7. That should be enough for D9 without overcomplicating the first version of the dashboard.

From a quality and audit perspective, I would like A5 to include at least two KPIs: number of incidents per 100 units and percentage of audit findings closed on time. These can be derived from A7 and the processes under T8 and T12. They will help us track whether the remediation actions agreed in D8 are effective.

Agreed on keeping the KPI set focused. For D9, my proposal is that A5 includes: 1) occupancy rate and rent per unit, 2) tenant satisfaction score, 3) service response time and backlog, 4) the two quality KPIs mentioned, 5) the sustainability and ICT KPIs suggested, and 6) a simple financial view of cost and savings from A2 and T11. That would give us a balanced view without being too heavy.

On the dashboard structure for D9, I would like A5 to have a simple top level view for the board, with a small number of headline KPIs and a traffic light status, and then more detail available for the working group. Monthly reporting is fine, with the option to look at weekly data for pilots if needed. As long as the data sources are clear and stable, I am comfortable with the set you proposed.

I can adjust A5 to show a top level board view with the headline KPIs and a more detailed working group view underneath. For reporting cadence, we can set monthly formal reports for the board and use the weekly async updates in this channel for the working group. That would align with the governance we defined in A8 and T9.

The proposed KPIs are workable from an operations standpoint, as long as we get some support to standardise data collection, especially for tenant satisfaction. For D9, I am fine with this set, provided we can automate as much of the data flow as possible over time.

I confirm that we can provide the sustainability and ICT KPIs from the systems we are planning under T3 and T7. For D9, I would just note that in the first months we may have data only for the pilot properties, and then expand as we roll out.

I am aligned with the quality KPIs and can ensure that A7 and the processes under T8 and T12 capture the necessary data. For D9, this will give us a clear view of whether the checklist A4 and remediation actions are working.

Given the alignment, I am ready to confirm D9. We will adopt the KPI set and dashboard structure you described in A5, with a board level view and a working group view, monthly formal reporting, and weekly updates in this channel. Please finalise A5 accordingly and ensure data owners are clear for each KPI.

I will update A5 to reflect D9 and assign data owners for each KPI, coordinating with housing, quality, and ICT. Now we should turn to the budget envelope and phasing for D10, based on the scenarios in T10 and the efficiency gains modelled in T11.

On budget, I have outlined three scenarios in T10: conservative, base, and accelerated. All respect the capex constraint in the first 12 months. The base scenario funds the agreed phase 1 pilots, the green ICT initiatives in D5, and the priority remediation actions from D8. The accelerated scenario brings forward some additional sustainability upgrades. I recommend we adopt the base scenario for D10, with a small contingency for unforeseen remediation.

From an operations view, the base scenario seems realistic. It gives us enough budget to address the key issues in the pilots and support the ICT rollout without stretching site teams too thin. The accelerated scenario might be hard to absorb operationally in the first year.

For ICT, the base scenario covers the phase 1 initiatives we agreed in D5 and allows for careful integration work under T3. The accelerated scenario would require more ICT capacity and could increase integration risk. I support using the base scenario for D10.

From the quality and remediation side, the base scenario funds the immediate safety fixes and key service improvements identified in A7. Some of the lower priority sustainability upgrades can wait for later phases. I am comfortable with that trade off for D10.

Taking into account your inputs and the board expectations, I will confirm D10 as follows: we adopt the base budget scenario in T10 for the first year, funding the phase 1 pilots, the agreed green ICT initiatives, and the priority remediation actions, with a modest contingency. Phasing by quarter will follow the pilot schedule and the roadmap in A3. Please ensure A2 and T10 are updated to reflect this decision.

I will update A2 and T10 to reflect D10 and align the financial model with the base scenario. I will also adjust T11 so that the efficiency gains are modelled against this phasing and feed into the KPIs in A5.
